status_effects.explanation: Odette's credibility is diminished as her confession exposes a habitual pattern of lying, though the narrator tempers this by noting she acted from timidity and lacked awareness of the harm caused.
M. Verdurin's attempt to manipulate the fidèles for his own comfort casts him unfavorably, though the scheme is mentioned only briefly and ultimately fails.

appraisal_events.evidence: « elle lui mentait déjà ! » ... « combien devait-il y en avoir eu d'autres, receleurs eux aussi d'un mensonge que Swann n'avait pas soupçonné. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator establishes that Odette had been habitually lying to Swann even during their happiest early months, exposing a pattern of concealment that undermines her trustworthiness, independent of the immediate Forcheville revelation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Bien que M. Verdurin eût cherché à persuader au pianiste et au docteur Cottard que la tante de l'un et les malades de l'autre n'avaient aucun besoin d'eux... il fut obligé de leur rendre leur liberté à Constantinople. »
appraisal_events.explanation: M. Verdurin is portrayed as manipulatively trying to keep the pianist and Dr. Cottard away from their real obligations for his own convenience, casting him in an unflattering light, and his scheme is ultimately overridden.
